types.name: Fenrir::Colour
types.doc: A colour as linear red, green, blue and alpha, each a float, usually in [0, 1] (ADR-0025). Debug draw, materials and lights take it, and the renderer packs it for vertices. Colours written as sRGB hex values, as colour pickers and art tools give them, are converted when made (FromSrgb). Default constructed, it is opaque white.

types.name: Fenrir::AmbientLight
types.doc: The constant light every lit surface receives, a scene resource (ADR-0024). A scene without one is lit by a default AmbientLight, a dim grey.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on the colour.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Image>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip` or `BoneMask`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. types.name: Fenrir::BackgroundType
types.doc: Which kind of background a CameraBackground holds.

types.name: Fenrir::ColourBackground
types.doc: A camera background of one colour, overriding the scene's.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. Black by default (Colour::Black).

types.name: Fenrir::SceneBackground
types.doc: A camera background that is the scene's own: its Sky.

types.name: Fenrir::CameraBackground
types.doc: What a camera's view shows where nothing was drawn: exactly one of SceneBackground and ColourBackground, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape. Assign a kind to change it (`camera.background = ColourBackground{Colour::Blue}`); read it through the checked view. Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::Orthographic
types.doc: An orthographic projection with reversed-Z depth (ADR-0026): the near plane maps to depth 1 and the far plane to 0. The width comes from the height and the viewport's pixel size.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: The full height of what the view shows, in world units.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: The distance to the near plane along the camera's -Z, in world units.

fields.name: far
fields.doc: The distance to the far plane along the camera's -Z, in world units.

types.name: Fenrir::Perspective
types.doc: A perspective projection with an infinite far plane and reversed-Z depth (ADR-0026): the near plane maps to depth 1 and the distance to 0. The aspect comes from the viewport's pixel size.

fields.name: verticalFov
fields.doc: The vertical field of view in radians; 60 degrees by default.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: The distance to the near plane, in world units.

types.name: Fenrir::ProjectionType
types.doc: Which kind of projection a Projection holds.

types.name: Fenrir::Projection
types.doc:
A camera's projection: exactly one of Perspective and Orthographic, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape.

Assign a kind to change it (`camera.projection = Orthographic{20.0f}`); read or edit it through the checked view (`camera.projection.As<Perspective>().verticalFov = 1.2f`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::ImageTarget
types.doc: A camera drawing into an image (ADR-0026): an RGBA8 sRGB ImageData with a size and no pixels, made with the asset store's Add and resized with Replace. Materials sample it like any image.

types.name: Fenrir::RenderTargetType
types.doc: Which kind of render target a RenderTarget holds.

types.name: Fenrir::WindowId
types.doc: Which window an input came from. A plain number chosen by whoever feeds the input (FenrirWindow, which keys its windows by it, or a test); FenrirInput only compares it.

types.name: Fenrir::WindowTarget
types.doc: A camera drawing into a window. The foundation renderer draws to the main window only.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: The main window by default (Window::MainWindow()). A camera naming another window is not drawn.

types.name: Fenrir::RenderTarget
types.doc: Where a camera's view goes: exactly one of WindowTarget and ImageTarget, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape. Assign a kind to change it (`camera.target = ImageTarget{image}`); read it through the checked view (`camera.target.As<ImageTarget>().image`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::Viewport
types.doc: The rectangle of its render target a view draws into, as fractions of the target's width and height from its top-left corner. The whole target by default.

types.name: Fenrir::Camera
types.doc:
Makes a view of the active scene from its entity, looking along the entity's local -Z with +Y up (ADR-0026). Plain data. Every enabled camera in the active scene draws one view a frame, into its viewport of its render target. Views into one target draw by `order`, lowest first, and ties by entity id, logged once. Each view has its own scene targets, and writes only its viewport.

Not drawn, logged once: a camera targeting a window other than the main window, a viewport under one pixel, or a target image that is stale, empty or not a render target. A minimised window draws nothing. A window no camera draws into is cleared to black, logged once.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: False draws no view.

fields.name: order
fields.doc: Views into one target draw lowest order first, so a higher order draws over a lower one.

fields.name: drawDebug
fields.doc: Whether the view draws the scene's debug shapes and world text (ADR-0025). Screen text and messages belong to the window, not the view, and draw either way.

types.name: Fenrir::ColourSky
types.doc: A sky of one colour.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. A dark grey by default, the sky of a scene with none.

types.name: Fenrir::CubemapSky
types.doc: A sky drawn from a cubemap image (ImageShape::Cubemap, such as one loaded from a `.cubemap` file), sampled by the direction each pixel looks along, so it stays put as the camera moves and turns with it.

types.name: Fenrir::DirectionalLight
types.doc: The light shining along its entity's world -Z (ADR-0024). The renderer uses the first one in the active scene and warns once if there are more.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. White by default (Colour::White).

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on the colour.

types.name: Fenrir::Entity
types.doc: Entity class that is used to interact with the entity list. This forms the basis of the ECS

types.name: Fenrir::Math::Ray
types.doc: Represents a ray in 3D space defined by an origin point and a direction vector.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: The origin point of the ray.

fields.name: dir
fields.doc: The direction vector of the ray, should be normalized to represent a direction.

types.name: Fenrir::MeshRenderer
types.doc:
Draws one mesh with one material at its entity's world transform (ADR-0023): one MeshRenderer, one draw. Plain data, read by the renderer from the active scene every Render; a mesh with several materials is several child entities, each with its own MeshRenderer.

An empty or stale mesh is skipped (a stale one logged once per handle). An empty or stale material draws with the fallback material, flat magenta and unlit, logged once per handle. An entity with no Transform draws at the origin.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: False hides this entity only; its children are drawn as their own MeshRenderers say.

types.name: Fenrir::RendererStats
types.doc: What the renderer did in its last drawn frame (ADR-0023).

fields.name: draws
fields.doc: Draws of MeshRenderers, one per item per view.

fields.name: passes
fields.doc: Render passes run.

fields.name: uploads
fields.doc: Assets uploaded to the GPU by the prepare step: a mesh, or a material's parameter block.

fields.name: paletteBytesUploaded
fields.doc: Bytes copied into the frame's palette buffer: every skeleton palette the frame's draws read.

fields.name: distinctPalettesWritten
fields.doc: Skeleton palettes written, one per skeleton and pose however many meshes and views draw it (ADR-0035).

fields.name: skinnedDraws
fields.doc: Draws of skinned MeshRenderers, one per item per view; part of `draws`.

types.name: Fenrir::SkinnedMesh
types.doc:
Skins the MeshRenderer beside it from a skeleton's pose (ADR-0035): plain data naming the skeleton entity, the entity carrying FenrirSkeleton's `SkeletonPose`. The mesh is drawn on the GPU from that skeleton's palette.

**A skinned item is drawn with the skeleton entity's world matrix. The mesh entity's own Transform and its ancestors are never applied**, unlike an ordinary MeshRenderer's: the mesh's vertices are already in the skeleton's bind space. `visible` and the material stay on the mesh entity's MeshRenderer. SpawnModel makes each skinned mesh entity a child of its skeleton entity at the identity, so the hierarchy reads naturally.

A mesh with skin data and no SkinnedMesh is not drawn; nor is one whose skeleton entity is dead, has no `SkeletonPose` or is not `Ready`, whose skeleton it was not baked for (more bones than the skeleton has, or a different bind signature), or when no skinning source is registered (FenrirSkeleton is not installed). A user shader without the `SKINNED` key draws it with the fallback material. Each is logged once as a warning. A SkinnedMesh on a mesh with no skin data is ignored, and the mesh draws rigidly (logged once).

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity whose pose skins the mesh.

types.name: Fenrir::SkyType
types.doc: Which kind of sky a Sky holds.

types.name: Fenrir::Sky
types.doc:
What a scene shows where nothing was drawn, a scene resource beside AmbientLight (ADR-0026): exactly one of ColourSky and CubemapSky, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape. A scene without one has the default ColourSky, a dark grey. Each camera whose background is SceneBackground draws it; a ColourBackground overrides it for that camera's view.

A cubemap that is empty, stale or not a cubemap with pixels draws the default ColourSky instead, logged once. Assign a kind to change it (`sky = CubemapSky{cubemap}`); read it through the checked view. Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.
